findings.description: __aexit__ ignores the received exception arguments and calls self.__exit__(None, None, None) instead of forwarding exc_type, exc_value and traceback.
findings.rationale: Trigger: an exception raised inside an `async with` attempt block. The exception info is dropped, so the attempt is recorded as a success (set_result(None)) and the failure is never recorded. Impact: retries do not happen for failed attempts and the result is silently wrong. The sync __exit__ presumably relies on exc_type/exc_value to call set_exception.
